sections.h2: Utility assessments come first in Cape Coral
sections.html:
The question buyers raise most here is whether your special assessment is paid. Cape Coral began as a 1957 land-sales platting laced with canals, and the city has been pushing water, sewer and irrigation lines out to parcels that never had them. Those extensions are repaid through special assessments.

The city's budget book describes more than 400 miles of waterways reaching the Intracoastal Waterway and the Gulf of Mexico, so many sellers also have seawalls, docks and canal-front insurance questions. Those answers come from other offices, but the assessment question starts with the city's billing office.

  • Look up whether your street sits in a Utilities Extension Project area.
  • Check your tax bill for a non-ad valorem line from the city.
  • Ask whether city water and irrigation are already connected.

sections.h2: Do special assessments pass to the buyer?
sections.html:
Generally yes, because they attach to the lot. An unpaid assessment passes to the new owner, who takes over the remaining balance, unless it is paid in full first.

The charge is treated as a tax levy and is recorded with the Lee County Clerk as a notice, not as a mortgage-style lien. Hardship and deferral programs are the exception. They require a lien on the property, and those liens must be paid in full at closing.

Assessments appear once a year on the Lee County Tax Collector's tax bill, so skipping one carries the same risk as skipping any part of the bill: a tax certificate. Payoffs can be made by mail, in person at the cashier window at City Hall, or online through the city's page for tax-billed assessments.

The city charges by lot area, not by the value of the house, and it bills vacant lots as well as built ones.

The two Cape Coral line-extension charges
ChargeWho paysUnit used
UEP special assessmentEvery parcel in an approved project area, built or vacantPer equivalent lot of 5,000 square feet, or per parcel of 10,000
Contribution in aid of constructionParcels outside a project area where a developer already paid for linesEquivalent parcels of 10,000 square feet, times the rate set by council

Each project area has its own billing term and interest rate, listed on the city's special assessments page. The charge repays project costs, including financing fees, once the council approves the project. If you are selling to an investor, get the remaining balance and its end date from the city in writing.

It can matter. In May 2025 the city mailed letters to about 1,000 owners in a northeast water-shortage area served by the Mid-Hawthorn Aquifer, telling them to connect to city irrigation within 180 days under Ordinance 7-25. The rule applies only where city irrigation service is already available.

The city ties the rule to its joint plan with the South Florida Water Management District, which followed that agency's water shortage declaration in November 2023. Owners are charged for irrigation water when they connect or when 180 days pass, whichever comes first.

  • With in-ground sprinklers, you need a free permit and inspection to connect.
  • Without sprinklers, a Kit-A outdoor spigot is installed and no permit is needed.
  • A plumber does the work, and any damaged swale or road must be repaired before the permit closes.
  • Keep trees seven feet and palms five feet from utilities.
  • In a mapped eagle nest zone, no machine digging from October 15 to May 15. Hand digging is allowed.

If you got a letter and have not complied, tell your buyer and your closing agent. Without a letter, the rule does not touch you.

sections.h2: What does the Lee County calendar mean for a seller?
sections.html:
It sets the year's clock. Value is fixed as of January 1, exemption requests are due March 1, and the appraiser mails TRIM notices in August. Late exemption applications may be granted for the following year, and you can ask for an informal conference at any time to talk through a value.

The Lee County Tax Collector mails bills in November. Paying early earns a 4 percent discount that month, dropping monthly to 1 percent in February, and anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

A TRIM notice lists proposed levies and any proposed or adopted non-ad valorem assessments, which is where a city utility charge would show up. Read that line before you set a price, then ask the city's customer billing office to confirm the balance in writing. That office also handles new construction and project questions.

Vacant lots in the same project area are assessed too, so a lot next door is not exempt. Talk to the title agent early so the payoff or the transfer of the balance is written into the contract.

Time gets short once a foreclosure judgment is entered. The public sale is set 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to more, with two weeks of notice first. A lender may instead ask for an order to show cause, and a homestead exemption on the latest roll is presumed to mean the home is owner-occupied. Call a Florida attorney if either has begun.

If someone is living in a vacant house without permission, an owner or agent can file a verified complaint with the sheriff to remove persons unlawfully occupying residential property. It requires no tenancy, no family tie, a property closed to the public, a demand to leave and no pending suit. A false statement can cost up to triple the fair market rent.

Several programs exist, depending on age and service. A city or county ordinance may add a homestead break for owners 65 and older within an income limit. Owners 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a discount equal to their VA rating. A disabled ex-servicemember may get a flat $5,000 cut in assessed value.

You can also ask the Tax Collector about deferral on Form DR-570, filed by March 31 after the assessment year. Find out which programs your household meets before you sell under pressure.

sections.h2: What belongs in the folder for a Cape Coral buyer?
sections.html:
• Your latest Lee County tax bill, with its non-ad valorem lines.
  • City utility status: connected, assessed, or not yet extended.
  • A recorded deed copy from the Clerk.
  • Payoff letters for loans, liens and association balances.
  • Permit records for roofs, windows, docks or additions.

Deed stamp tax in Lee County runs at the standard seventy cent rate, and every signer is liable. Recording is charged per page under section 28.24.

Hand the folder to the title agent early. A buyer who sees the assessment balance and permit records up front has fewer reasons to renegotiate after the inspection, and a seller who can answer those questions the same day keeps a quick sale on schedule.

faqs.q: Does a Cape Coral utility assessment stay with the house?
faqs.a: Yes, if unpaid. The new owner assumes the remaining balance, except that hardship and deferral liens must be paid at closing.

faqs.q: Where is a Cape Coral assessment billed?
faqs.a: On the annual Lee County Tax Collector bill, as a non-ad valorem line. Payoffs can also be made at City Hall or online.

faqs.q: Who gets the irrigation connection letters?
faqs.a: Only owners in the northeast water-shortage area where city irrigation is already available. The city mailed about 1,000 in May 2025.

faqs.q: When must I file for homestead in Lee County?
faqs.a: By March 1 of the tax year, with the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

faqs.q: Can I remove someone living in my vacant Cape Coral house?
faqs.a: Possibly, through the sheriff complaint process if the statutory conditions are met, such as no tenancy and a prior demand to leave. Talk to an attorney first.
